the_ruling_verbatim: record of truth is not a goodness later on when it confuses you. fix it
now_the_spec_says: A record of truth is corrected once it stops being evidence and becomes a trap. The test: does the edit destroy evidence, or destroy a trap? A dead identifier is no evidence — it is a live-looking pointer to nothing. Correct it, keeping what it said and who corrected it.
the_reason_that_dies: No file dies. What dies is a REFLEX of CC's that had hardened into a rule nobody ruled: 'a berth is a record of truth and may not be edited to look consistent.' That sentence is true about its real target — collapsing an error into a coherent shape, which Law 7 forbids — and CC had been applying it one level too wide, to any edit of any berth for any reason, including edits that remove nothing but a broken pointer. Applied at that width it stops being Law 7 and becomes preservation for its own sake, which is exactly the goodness Akien denies: the record was kept intact and the later reader was confused, which is a cost with no purchase. The immediate instance: the sorted berth for this ticket was cast spelling the id `the-shim-builds-a-piece`; Akien corrected the name to `aider-builds-a-piece` the same day; CC renamed the ticket and then deliberately LEFT the berth pointing at a filename that no longer exists, announcing the decision as a virtue.

THE TRACE, AND HE GAVE IT AT CONFIRMATION: 'and this too is CP4.' Not a new door — CP4 ('make everything suck less for everybody') is the TERMINAL goal, and Law 2 puts CP1-CP6 in the process that builds the system, so CP4 was always aimed at the corpus and not only at the software. A record kept intact that confuses a later reader is friction with nothing bought; preservation for its own sake is a cost charged to the reader forever. CP4 names the affected beings as 'living beings, ecosystems, AIs' — the reader whose friction this ruling removes is explicitly in that set. Same day, same CP: he ruled that the Laws themselves are reviewable when they chafe, and that is CP4 too, on the same reasoning.

THE OPEN EDGE FROM THE RETIRED PACKET IS CLOSED, AND NOT THE WAY IT WAS ASKED. The retired packet left one question live: does the evidence-vs-trap test reach `history.json`? Akien answered it sideways on 2026-08-17 by moving the ground: 'history for a thing underway: good (and usually short). history beyond that, noise' and 'the repo is itself the state of the machine. history not needed to establish what's going on right now for some piece goes over in the other repo. we can still grep for it as needed.' So the question was not whether an old history note may be corrected — it was whether it should still be sitting in the reader's path. Law 5's restatement is the live work that answers it, and it is NOT settled by this packet.

THE CORRECTION AS PERFORMED, so a later reader can check it rather than trust it: berth sorted-20260817T102630-a049c8d5e854.json, both occurrences (answers.collision_check and one bullet), each rewritten to name the live id with a bracketed [CORRECTED 2026-08-17, by Akien] note carrying the dead spelling and the reason.
